title: Staff retreat and Townline playbook (rehearsal + fallback)
content:
Purpose
----
This is the single playbook for the December staff retreat week and the adjacent company townline (all-hands) rehearsal. The doc purpose: align on exec messaging, create a run-of-show that minimizes cognitive load for speakers, record fallback plans for tech/staffing issues, and capture final asks and decision owners coming out of the event.

Audience
----
- Execs and People Ops leads who will present or host sessions
- Event producers and AV team
- People managers charged with pre-read distribution and squad-level breakout prep
- Comms for follow-up comms and post-event artifacts

Top-level objectives (what success looks like)
----
1) Clear company-level narrative that ties product priorities (hosting, dedicated capacity, private deployments) to customer stories and measurable Q1 milestones.
2) All-hands run-of-show executes within the 75-minute window with <5 minute aggregate AV slippage.
3) At least three concrete cross-functional commitments captured in the decision log with named owners and Q1 due dates.
4) Rehearsal finishes with all speakers comfortable with transitions and fallback cues.

Key messaging pillars (short blurbs for slides / talking points)
----
- Developer-first focus: We make inference predictable and cost-effective for builders.
- Serving over ownership: our advantage is in production-grade serving and economics.
- Multi-mode availability: hosted, dedicated, private — same API, consistent controls.
- Q1 anchor: improve median latency by 12% across popular embeddings flows and reduce per-1k-token cost by 8% with Optimize recommendations.

Run of show (75 min)
----
0:00–0:05 Welcome & framing — Host (People Ops)
0:05–0:20 CEO update (strategy + market signal) — focus on thesis and where we win
0:20–0:30 Product highlight (Hosted API improvements + migration story) — Product Lead
0:30–0:40 Engineering snapshot (Serving runtime wins & SLO progress) — Eng VP
0:40–0:50 Customer story (case study, short video) — Solutions Eng / Customer Success
0:50–0:60 Ops & reliability (Dedicated and Private operational milestones) — SRE Lead
0:60–0:70 Roadmap & asks (Clear Q1 asks to teams + OKR preview) — Head of Product
0:70–0:75 Close & CTA (how to get involved, Q&A prompt) — CEO + People Ops

Rehearsal schedule (detailed)
----
- 4 days out: Tech check — AV lead confirms slide links, video playback, stage mic routing.
- 2 days out: Speaker slide lock deadline (final deck due).
- 1 day out: Full run-through on stage with presenter order, transitions, and timing. Each speaker practices opening and closing lines and the one line that connects to the next presenter.
- Same day (2 hours before): Backstage check, final mic check, prompter sync.

Speaker prep checklist
----
- One-slide personal opener (who I am + 1 line tying to company thesis).
- One-sentence headline for your section (prep for prompter).
- 3x bullets under each headline (no more than 12 words each).
- 1 explicit transition sentence to the next speaker.
- Upload deck to shared slides with final name convention: [lastname]-[role]-final.pptx

Slide & asset checklist (for AV/Comms)
----
- Master deck (speaker order + time stamps)
- Speaker deck exports for prompter (pdf)
- Customer video clip (encoded H.264, 1080p)
- Speaker headshots + titles for lower-third graphics
- CI/brand-approved last slide with CTAs + follow-up links

Fallbacks (concise)
----
- If AV fails for a speaker: give them a wireless lav and move to presenter remote. If both fail, run speaker audio over Zoom link and keep the slide deck advancing manually from console.
- If CEO is delayed: Head of Product to briefly re-anchor with 3-min update and CEO joins in Q&A slot.
- If customer video playback fails: show static slide with transcript + live read by Solutions Eng. Capture the video and follow up via post-event email.
- If timing runs long (>3 min over at half) : cut the optional product demo and shift to 1-min highlights for remaining sections.

Decision log (to be filled live)
----
- Commitment 1: Reduce embeddings median latency by 12% (owner: Eng VP, due: 2026-03-31)
- Commitment 2: Launch pilot of Dedicated burst pools in EU (owner: Head of Dedicated, due: 2026-02-28)
- Commitment 3: Two cross-team eval prompts for Optimize signoff (owner: Applied ML lead, due: 2026-02-15)
(Note: these rows are a template — team leads will confirm final owners in rehearsal)

Q&A bucket (anticipated tough questions + suggested answers)
----
Q: How are we balancing cost vs latency when recommending quantized models?
A: We recommend quantization profiles per workload; Optimize will surface expected unit-cost delta and quality regression metrics to let teams choose.

Q: What happens to customers on older model variants during rollouts?
A: Smart routing + automatic fallback ensures compatibility; Dedicated customers can pin versions for up to 90 days.

Pre-read (what to send 3 days before)
----
- Final deck (pdf)
- 1-pager: event objectives + one-line asks from execs
- Operational notes: arrival, parking, AV contact, rehearsal times
- Short poll: preference for in-person vs fully-remote breakout format

Post-event artifacts & comms plan
----
- 24–48h: Send recording + short highlights (3 min clip) + decisions and owners note.
- 1 week: Release detailed action tracker with milestones and owners imported into Jira.
- 4 weeks: Check-in retrospective (what worked / what didn’t) and impact signals for OKRs.

Open questions (needs input before finalizing)
----
- Confirm whether we want the CEO to reveal the Q1 OKR north star live, or save it for the staff email to avoid surprise to partners. (input: CEO/Comms)
- Decide on the cadence for follow-up: weekly updates vs biweekly depending on owner load. (input: Owners)
- Are there any legal/customer approvals required before showing the customer clip? (input: Legal / CS)
notes: Working doc — contains rehearsal timing and fallback guidance; not the final post to staff. Use during runbook handoff.
